package.title: How Does a Semaglutide Pill Survive Your Stomach? #shorts
package.description:
A helper molecule called SNAC buffers stomach acid around the semaglutide pill (Wegovy), helps protect it from the enzyme pepsin and helps it absorb through the stomach lining. social.instagram_caption:
Your stomach vs. this pill 💊

Semaglutide is a peptide — and your stomach is built to break those down. So how does the Wegovy pill survive?

A helper molecule called SNAC does 3 jobs right where the tablet dissolves:
🔹 Buffers stomach acid around the tablet
🔹 Helps protect semaglutide from the enzyme pepsin
🔹 Helps it absorb through the stomach lining

The catch: only a small share reaches your bloodstream. The label for Rybelsus, the diabetes version that also uses SNAC, estimates about 0.4–1%.

Does it still work? In the OASIS 4 trial, adults with overweight or obesity lost 13.6% of body weight on average over 64 weeks vs. 2.2% on placebo. The weekly injection, in STEP 1, showed 14.9% vs. 2.4% over 68 weeks — separate trials, not head-to-head, but a similar range. Nausea and other stomach side effects were the most common, mostly mild to moderate.

factcheck.summary: The script is accurate and safe, so it passes with three minor wording fixes. I checked every number against its source. (1) Buckley et al., Sci Transl Med 2018, studied people and dogs. It found that SNAC raises the pH right around the tablet, which shuts down pepsin and protects semaglutide. SNAC also briefly helps the drug cross the stomach lining. That matches the three steps in s3 (buffer → protect → absorb), and s3 correctly says the protection follows from the buffering. (2) The Rybelsus prescribing information puts absolute oral bioavailability at about 0.4% to 1%. The script credits this to the Rybelsus label and doesn't claim it for the Wegovy pill, so the attribution is honest. SNAC is in both products. (3) OASIS 4 (Wharton et al., NEJM 2025) reports −13.6% vs −2.2% at week 64. GI adverse events were the most common, at 74.0% vs 42.2%, mostly mild to moderate. (4) STEP 1 (Wilding et al., NEJM 2021) reports −14.9% vs −2.4% at 68 weeks. The pill-vs-shot comparison is clearly labelled as separate trials, not head-to-head. FDA approved the Wegovy pill on December 22, 2025, so calling it 'the Wegovy pill' is accurate. The script gives no dosing, no switching advice and no sourcing advice, and it includes the prescriber line. It is about 150 words, which is under the 170-word limit. The hook's question is answered by about 8 s.

issues.claim: Semaglutide is a peptide. Your stomach is built to destroy those.
issues.problem: Slight overstatement. Acid and pepsin start breaking proteins down in the stomach, but most protein digestion happens in the small intestine. 'Destroy' is also a bit fear-toned for the brand voice.
issues.fix: Semaglutide is a peptide. Your stomach is built to break those down. So how does the Wegovy pill survive?

issues.claim: The label for Rybelsus... estimates about 0.4 to 1%.
issues.problem: Accurate, but it doesn't say what the percentage measures. 'Gets in' could be heard as something other than the share that reaches the bloodstream.
issues.fix: Here's the catch: only a small share reaches your bloodstream. The label for Rybelsus, the diabetes version that also uses SNAC, estimates about 0.4 to 1%.

issues.claim: Full pill-versus-shot breakdown on our channel.
issues.problem: This promises a long-form video that may not exist yet. If no such video has been published, the CTA misleads viewers.
issues.fix: Keep the line only if a pill-vs-shot long-form video is already live. Otherwise use: "Follow @InforMedLab for more on how GLP-1 works. And talk to your doctor or prescriber about whether it's right for you."
